subject: Acme - SLO/SLA language and latency measurement follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@acme.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Acme - post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier  great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock SLO/SLA language into the contract draft: 

1) Performance targets you mentioned: p95 latency <= 150ms for single-turn text generation (non-streaming) at your baseline concurrency (200 concurrent requests). You also called out a target throughput of ~400 req/s sustained with bursts to 700 req/s for short windows.

2) Streaming: important for your product  key requirement is first-byte latency on streaming responses (you care about how fast a partial reply appears), plus stable chunking cadence. You said stream-first-byte p95 should be <= 120ms and per-chunk processing latency <= 50ms average.

3) Measurement & scope: you asked whether our latency measurement includes network time, and how we compute windowing (rolling vs calendar). We owe you clear language on: measurement method, exclusions (maintenance, DDoS, customer network), reporting cadence (weekly summary + monthly SLA report), and remedies (service credits).

Proposed next steps:
- I'll attach a draft SLA section with measurement definitions and suggested exclusions (attached).
- Can we confirm the precise concurrency numbers and a 30-day rolling window for SLO evaluation? (Tom/SRE)
- I'll loop in Vivek to confirm the server-side measurement points and to propose a clear sentence on what we exclude.

I'll follow up with the draft SLA attached. Please flag anything that looks off.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: acme_ma_sla_draft.pdf (SLA draft, 3 pages)

From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>, Acme SRE Team <sre@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme - post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Thanks Marissa  that matches our notes. A few clarifying items before we loop Legal: 

- For non-streaming p95 <= 150ms: is that measured from request arrival at Redwood ingress to final byte sent (server-side only), or is it end-to-end including our network? We need the latter for customer-facing SLAs, but understand that can be tricky.
- For streaming, we care about first-byte to first chunk and then chunk cadence. Can you confirm whether your per-chunk numbers are averaged across chunks or measured per-chunk percentile?
- Exclusions: we expect planned maintenance windows to be excluded, and obvious customer-network outages. Curious if Redwood excludes traffic surges due to customer-triggered spikes or if those count against the SLO.
- Reporting cadence: weekly summary is fine; for contract we prefer monthly rolling window and an automated monthly SLA report.

If you can confirm these points and tweak the draft, we can circulate to our procurement/legal.

Appreciate it,
Sara
Sr. Product Manager, Acme Corp
--

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Acme - post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Looping in with engineering measurement details  summary below (happy to expand into precise contract wording):

- Measurement point: We measure latency server-side at the Redwood ingress (time request received by our front proxy) to the time the final byte of the response is emitted by our service. That excludes the customer's last-mile/WAN latency. For streaming we track: (a) time to first-byte (TTFB) from ingress to first outbound chunk; (b) per-chunk processing time measured as delta between chunk emission events on our egress.
- Percentiles: SLOs are typically stated on p95 for non-streaming requests (as you requested). For streaming, first-byte p95 is reasonable; per-chunk we recommend using median/avg for cadence SLAs and p95 for stall detection.
- Windowing: We recommend a 30-day rolling window for SLO evaluation. This avoids calendar boundary artifacts and is standard for production SLAs.
- Exclusions: Planned maintenance and provider-side network incidents affecting our regions should be excluded. Customer-side network failures (e.g., errors between Acme network and our ingress) are excluded from Redwood measurement but we can provide logs. For customer-triggered traffic surges: unless the customer purchases burst protection or a dedicated capacity pool, spikes count against the SLO. For Dedicated/Committed lanes we can add explicit burst handling.
- Remedies: We provide service credits tied to monthly breach percentage thresholds. Exact language I can draft with Legal  typically tiered credits (5% credit for X% breach, 10% for higher).

I can add a short paragraph that explicitly defines the ingress/egress measurement points for the draft SLA.

- Vivek
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@acme.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme - post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Thanks Vivek  that's super helpful. Attached is an updated SLA section that incorporates Vivek's language and proposes:

- Measurement definition: "Latency is measured at Redwood's ingress: the interval between time of request receipt by Redwood's front proxy and the time the final byte of the response is emitted by Redwood's service. For streaming responses, 'first-byte latency' is measured from ingress to the time the first chunk is emitted; per-chunk latency is measured between consecutive chunk emit events."
- Window: 30-day rolling window for SLO evaluation.
- Exclusions: Planned maintenance (scheduled with >=48h notice), force majeure, customer network outages, and attacks (DDoS) that are clearly not the result of Redwood infrastructure.
- Remedies: Monthly service credits on verified breaches (proposed tiers in attachment).

Lauren  can you review the proposed exclusions and remedies language (in the attached PDF)? Sara/Tom  can you confirm the concurrency/throughput numbers (200 concurrent baseline, 400 req/s sustained, burst to 700) so I can lock those into section 2.

Thanks  I'll stand by for quick feedback and then we can push to procurement.

--
Marissa

Attachments: acme_ma_sla_draft.pdf (updated), latency_measurement_table.xlsx

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Sara Kim <sara.kim@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme - post-call recap: performance targets & next steps

Reviewed the draft. A few suggested edits to make the SLA contract-ready: 

- Remedies: Recommend specifying "service credit up to X% per month" and a maximum aggregate cap (e.g., credits not to exceed 50% of monthly fees) to keep commercial risk bounded.
- Exclusions: Add a clause that Redwood will provide evidence/logs for incidents claimed as excluded; this helps prevent ambiguous exclusions.
- Measurement: For customer-facing SLA we should offer two options: (1) Redwood-measured (server-side) SLA as drafted, or (2) end-to-end measured SLA where Acme supplies a synthetic probe and we jointly agree on probe locations \u2014 the latter carries higher variance and should have adjusted thresholds. Suggest we include both as options in the contract language.

I'll prepare a redline and send to Legal. If Acme prefers end-to-end, Procurement will need to accept the adjusted targets.

- Lauren
Head of Legal (Contracts), Redwood Inference
